correctness.rationale: For any compatible metric \(d\) on the compact countable product, uniform equivalence with a standard summable product metric gives a finite coordinate prefix whose equality forces \(d<\varepsilon\). Infinitely many non-singleton factors supply a distinct pair differing only beyond that prefix. Coordinatewise dynamics preserve equality of the prefix for every group element, so that same pair stays \(\varepsilon\)-close under the whole group. The horoball conclusion is therefore immediate for every horofunction. The expansiveness boundary follows: infinitely many non-singletons forbid any expansivity constant, while a finite product is expansive exactly when each non-singleton factor is expansive.
residual_risks: The proof uses compact metrizability and coordinatewise action; it does not extend verbatim to nonmetrizable uncountable products or coupled skew products.
